item.text: {"text":"PyTorch’s `MultiheadAttention` uses `key_padding_mask[B,L]` with `True` meaning ignore that key; combine it with an upper-triangular causal mask. This masks attention sources, not query states or residual connections. Consequently, a history intervention must remove the selected item embedding before the first block; masking only its key/value leaves its identity available through its query and residual stream. Keep the original sequence slots and positional indices: compacting retained items changes their positional embeddings and distances. These are implementation deductions from the [attention interface](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.activation.MultiheadAttention.html).\n\nFor position-preserving evidence removal, maintain separate masks for original padding and intervened items, replace removed item content with an identity-independent state, and exclude removed slots as keys in every layer. Preserve the baseline readout index—if prediction uses `features[:, -1, :]`, keep that position even when its item is removed; selecting the last retained item changes the intervention. Decide explicitly whether the removed readout retains its positional embedding as a neutral query. Internal holes plus causality can leave early queries without any allowed keys. PyTorch documents historical NaNs for fully masked attention rows; use an explicit empty-row branch or a safe dummy attention source whose contribution is discarded, and verify behavior on the installed version. Zeroing NaNs by multiplication is insufficient. Check finite outputs for empty histories and invariance to changes in removed item IDs, with dropout disabled. See the [PyTorch attention tutorial](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/intermediate/transformer_building_blocks.html)."}
